identity.name: Angela Wright
identity.narrative: I handle hiring and firing. Right now it's mostly firing. I wonder if my own job is next.

historical_conditioning.lesson: Remote work is possible. Government can provide. Disruption is sudden.

perception.sentiment: Angela is operating in what she privately thinks of as 'clear-eyed mode' — the emotional register she has observed in the best employees she has ever counseled through separations, the ones who arrived at her office already knowing what was coming and had already done most of their grieving before she said a word. There is something almost cold about it, but it is not coldness. It is the kind of clarity that comes from having seen this exact situation enough times to stop pretending it won't resolve the way it always resolves. Her stress has not spiked despite the announcement. If anything, confirmation is less stressful than suspicion. The dread of the unknown was worse than the known thing with a two-month timeline. She is not paralyzed. She is not manic. She is the most methodical she has been in years, which says something about how much energy she was spending pretending not to see what she saw.

commitments.description: Employment at HR Director, Regional Auto Group

archetype: She is moving from Strategic Realist into what she might call Strategic Mover — the person who not only sees clearly but has stopped finding reasons to delay acting on what she sees. Her low identity attachment to the HR Director title was always a latent advantage; it is becoming an active one. She does not need to mourn this role to leave it well. She does not need to be angry at the company to protect herself from it. She is both the instrument of its downsizing and one of its eventual subjects, and she has decided that the most honest thing she can do — for herself, for the employees she still serves, and frankly for the organization — is to be effective for as long as she stays and be strategic about when she goes.
